title: Origami batcher: cost mapper and compact quant schematics
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduce Origami batcher (folding micro-batches for unit-econ gains), cost mapper service, and per-shard compact quant schematics. Rolling canary, no breaking API changes.
description: Summary: Adds a new batching strategy (Origami batcher) that dynamically folds short requests into shaped micro-batches to improve GPU slot utilization, a cost-mapper service that maps request signatures to unit-economics curves, and compact quant schematics (per-shard quant profiles and sensitivity maps) to enable safer automated quantization suggestions. Motivation: Many short, bursty workloads are paying high per-token unit cost because they miss batching/filling windows. Origami folds and groups compatible requests while respecting tail latency SLOs. The cost mapper gives a single source of truth for per-signature expected tokens, latency curve, and marginal cost so Optimize can recommend safe defaults. Compact quant schematics capture layer-wise sensitivity at a coarse granularity so we can safely propose 4/8-bit profiles grouped by shard.
design_notes:
- Origami batcher lives in runtime/batcher and is a policy that can be enabled per-route. It uses a light-weight fingerprint (route+prefix-hash+seq-dist) to decide foldability and a window-based scheduler to form shaped micro-batches. The folding policy is conservative by default: it only folds when expected added latency < 6ms and expected unit-econ improvement > 5%.
- Cost mapper (runtime/metrics/cost_mapper.py) consumes token histograms + per-model latency lookup and exposes a gRPC endpoint for Optimize to query expected unit cost and risk band. It stores compact histograms (50 buckets) to keep memory low.
- Compact quant schematics are YAML manifests under optimize/quant/schematics/. Each schematic describes per-shard quant tier, layer-sensitivity bucket, and recommended runtime flags. The schematics are generated by a new calibration tool (optimize/quant/schematic_generator.py) that runs on a small validation corpus and emits sensitivity summaries.
migration_and_rollout: Rollout plan: 1) Feature gated off by default. 2) Canary on 3 dedicated hosts (redwood-dedicated-canary-1..3) with 1% traffic split via routing rule. 3) Run A/B for 48 hours comparing cost/unit and P95 latency on affected routes. 4) Gradual ramp to 20% if no regressions, followed by full rollout. Rollback: routing fallback to previous batcher and quant profile; cost-mapper calls are non-blocking and degrade to cached defaults.
testing: Unit tests for folding logic and cost-mapper histogram ingestion added. Integration perf tests: tests/perf/test_origami_profile.py (simulated short-request trace) and a nightly canary scenario in ci/workflows/perf.yml. Quality checks: end-to-end evals against held-out prompt sets to ensure model output similarity within threshold (BLEU/ROUGE and embedding distance). A small manual QA pass with Solutions Eng validated no visible semantic regressions on a sample of 120 prompts.
safety_and_fallbacks:
- Folding is opt-in per-route and can be disabled at runtime via route config.
- If cost-mapper fails, Optimize falls back to route-level defaults.
- Quant schematics marked 'suggested' by default; automated apply requires an explicit rollout from Optimize UI.
- Regression alerting added to Console: econ.delta > 10% or generation-similarity drop > configured threshold triggers automated rollback.

review_comments: Diego: Nice approach. Two questions: how does origami interact with KV-cache and streaming? Could folding increase KV-cache churn?

Maya: Reply: Origami only folds requests that share prefix-hash in the same folding window; we avoid folding across different cache keys. For streaming, we do not fold requests that have started streaming responses. Added a check in origami_batcher.py to skip streaming sessions.
Priya: Please add a safety gate that prevents folding for routes with < 10ms tail-SLO. Also add telemetry for folded vs unfurled latency distribution.
Maya: Added config 'min_tail_slo_ms' with default 20ms and telemetry counters folded_count/fold_failure_reason. Updated tests to cover SLO gating.
Eva: The quant schematic format looks good but please include a 'confidence' field so Optimize can rank suggestions.
Maya: Added 'confidence' as float [0-1] and updated generator to compute it from per-layer delta metrics.

merge_details: Merged by Diego Ramirez via squash-merge. Commit message: 'Origami batcher + cost-mapper + compact quant schematics: enable cost-aware folding and safer quant suggestions'. Changelog auto-updated under Optimize > Batching & Quant recommendations. Canaries monitored for 72h post-merge.
notes_for_ops:
- Add new env var ORIGAMI_ENABLED=false by default.
- Cost-mapper requires extra 250MB memory for histogram store on each serving host; expected CPU overhead < 2%.
- If you see increased kv-cache misses on canary, disable origami for affected routes and open SUP ticket.
